Usage notes:
- If there's already a CLAUDE.md, suggest improvements to it.
- When you make the initial CLAUDE.md, do not repeat yourself and do not include obvious instructions like "Provide helpful error messages to users", "Write unit tests for all new utilities", "Never include sensitive information (API keys, tokens) in code or commits".

- Don't include generic development practices.
- If there are Cursor rules (in .cursor/rules/ or .cursorrules) or Copilot rules (in .github/copilot-instructions.md), make sure to include the important parts.
- If there is a README.md, make sure to include the important parts.

- Be sure to prefix the file with the following text:

```
# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
```

This is a [Next.js](https://nextjs.org) project bootstrapped with [`create-next-app`](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/cli/create-next-app).

## Getting Started

First, run the development server:

```bash
npm run dev
# or
yarn dev
# or
pnpm dev
# or
bun dev
```

Open [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000) with your browser to see the result.

You can start editing the page by modifying `app/page.tsx`. The page auto-updates as you edit the file.

This project uses [`next/font`](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/optimizing/fonts) to automatically optimize and load [Geist](https://vercel.com/font), a new font family for Vercel.

## Learn More

To learn more about Next.js, take a look at the following resources:

- [Next.js Documentation](https://nextjs.org/docs) - learn about Next.js features and API.
- [Learn Next.js](https://nextjs.org/learn) - an interactive Next.js tutorial.

You can check out [the Next.js GitHub repository](https://github.com/vercel/next.js) - your feedback and contributions are welcome!

Perfect! Now I have a comprehensive understanding of the codebase. Let me create a detailed summary of the architecture:

## Pathway Next.js Codebase Architecture Summary

Based on my thorough exploration, here's a comprehensive analysis of the Pathway application architecture:

### 1. PROJECT STRUCTURE

The project follows a modern Next.js 16 structure with the following key directories:

```
src/
├── app/                          # Next.js App Router (primary routing)
│   ├── (auth)/                  # Route group for auth pages
│   │   ├── login/page.tsx
│   │   └── register/page.tsx
│   ├── category/[slug]/         # Category exploration by slug
│   ├── create/page.tsx          # Guide creation interface
│   ├── guide/[guideId]/[slug]/  # Guide detail view with nested routing
│   ├── profile/[username]/      # User profile pages
│   ├── layout.tsx               # Root layout with theme provider
│   ├── page.tsx                 # Home/explore page
│   └── globals.css              # Global Tailwind styles
├── components/                   # Reusable React components (39 files)
│   ├── comments/                # Comment thread components
│   ├── create/                  # Guide builder form components
│   ├── gallery/                 # Guide gallery/grid components
│   ├── guide/                   # Guide detail view components
│   ├── layout/                  # App shell, navbar, sidebar
│   ├── profile/                 # User profile components
│   ├── theme/                   # Theme provider & toggle
│   ├── timeline/                # Chat message timeline visualization
│   └── ui/                      # Base UI components (avatar, dialogs, video)
├── constants/                    # Application constants
│   └── categories.ts            # Predefined guide categories
├── hooks/                        # Custom React hooks
│   ├── use-auth.ts             # Authentication state management
│   └── use-guide-builder.tsx    # Guide builder state with useReducer
├── lib/                          # Utility functions and integrations
│   ├── supabase/
│   │   ├── client.ts           # Browser Supabase client (singleton)
│   │   ├── server.ts           # Server-side Supabase client
│   │   ├── auth.ts             # Auth server actions (signUp, signIn, signOut)
│   │   ├── middleware.ts       # Middleware for session updates
│   │   └── queries/
│   │       ├── guides.ts       # Guide CRUD & media operations
│   │       ├── guide-detail.ts # Guide detail fetching & interactions
│   │       ├── profile.ts      # Profile & user-specific queries
│   │       └── create-guide.ts # (inferred from imports)
│   ├── parser/
│   │   ├── claude-code.ts      # JSONL parser for Claude Code conversations
│   │   └── categorize-block.ts # Block categorization logic
│   ├── utils/
│   │   └── avatar.ts           # Avatar utilities
│   ├── utils.ts                # Common utilities (cn, formatting)
│   └── markdown.ts             # Markdown processing
├── types/
│   ├── database.ts             # Supabase auto-generated database types
│   └── index.ts                # Custom application types
├── middleware.ts                # Next.js middleware for auth session updates
└── supabase/                    # Supabase config (migrations, etc)
```

### 2. KEY ARCHITECTURAL PATTERNS

**Routing Architecture:**
- **App Router** (Modern): The primary routing system using directory-based routing in `app/`
- **Dynamic Routes**: Heavy use of `[params]` for IDs and slugs (e.g., `guide/[guideId]/[slug]`)
- **Route Groups**: Uses `(auth)` syntax for logical grouping of related routes
- **Client Components**: Most pages use `"use client"` for interactivity

**Data Fetching Patterns:**
- **Client-side fetching**: Pages use `useEffect` + state management for data in client components
- **Direct Supabase queries**: Browser client used directly from client components (potential performance concern for large datasets)
- **Server actions**: Auth operations (`signUp`, `signIn`, `signOut`) are server actions
- **Batch operations**: Large data inserts chunked in batches of 500

**State Management:**
- **React Context + useReducer**: `useGuideBuilder` hook for complex form state with nested steps/blocks
- **Local state with useState**: Used for UI state (sorting, loading, filters)
- **Custom hook abstraction**: `useAuth` encapsulates Supabase auth subscription logic

### 3. IMPORTANT CONFIGURATION FILES

**next.config.ts**
- Minimal configuration (currently empty/default)
- TypeScript configured for strict mode

**tsconfig.json**
- **Path alias**: `@/*` maps to `./src/*` for clean imports
- **Strict mode**: Enabled for type safety
- **Target**: ES2017 with React JSX transform
- **Module resolution**: bundler strategy

**eslint.config.mjs**
- Uses ESLint 9 with flat config
- Includes Next.js Core Web Vitals rules
- Includes TypeScript support
- Ignores `.next/`, `out/`, `build/`, `next-env.d.ts`

**postcss.config.mjs**
- Single plugin: `@tailwindcss/postcss` (Tailwind v4)

**Package.json Dependencies:**
- **Next.js 16.1.6**: Latest stable version with React 19.2.3
- **Supabase**: `@supabase/supabase-js` (client) + `@supabase/ssr` (server-side auth)
- **UI/Styling**: Tailwind CSS v4, Framer Motion, Lucide React icons, next-themes
- **Utilities**: clsx, tailwind-merge (for className merging)

### 4. SUPABASE INTEGRATION

**Authentication:**
- **Browser client** (`client.ts`): Singleton pattern for client-side operations
- **Server client** (`server.ts`): Cookie-based session management for server components
- **Middleware integration** (`middleware.ts`): Session validation on every request with cookie handling
- **Auth actions** (`auth.ts`): Server-side functions for `signUp`, `signIn`, `signOut`
- **Custom hook** (`useAuth`): Manages user state + profile loading with subscription cleanup

**Database Access Patterns:**
- **Type-safe queries**: Uses auto-generated `Database` type from Supabase
- **Nested queries**: Joins profiles, categories, media using Supabase's PostgREST syntax
- **Sorting**: Multiple sort options (recent, popular, trending, completed)
- **Pagination**: Limit-based pagination (currently 24 guides per page)
- **Batch operations**: Chunked inserts for large chat message batches
- **Soft deletes**: Uses `is_hidden` flag instead of hard deletes

**Core Database Tables:**
- **posts**: Main guide/content storage
- **profiles**: User information
- **categories**: Guide categories with icons
- **guide_steps**: Step-based guide structure
- **guide_blocks**: Parsed chat/code blocks from conversations
- **chat_messages**: Timeline of AI/human messages
- **comments**: Threaded comments with depth tracking
- **post_likes, post_saves, comment_likes**: Social interaction tracking
- **follows**: User follow relationships
- **post_media**: Images/videos associated with guides
- **timeline_chapters**: Named sections within guide timelines
- **message_annotations**: Author notes on specific messages
- **message_stars**: Starred messages in timelines

**Storage:**
- **Supabase Storage**: `post-media` bucket for guide images/videos
- **URL pattern**: `{userId}/{postId}/{mediaIndex}.{ext}`

### 5. COMPONENT ORGANIZATION

**Component Categories:**

| Category | Purpose | Example Files |
|----------|---------|----------------|
| **layout/** | App structure & navigation | AppShell, Navbar, Sidebar |
| **gallery/** | Guide browsing & discovery | GuideGrid, GuideCard, SortTabs |
| **create/** | Complex form builder | GuideBuilder, StepList, BlockPool |
| **guide/** | Guide viewing & interactions | GuidActions, Recommendations, MediaGallery |
| **comments/** | Discussion threads | CommentItem, CommentSection |
| **profile/** | User profiles | ProfileHeader, ProfileTabs, CommentList |
| **theme/** | Dark/light mode | ThemeProvider, ThemeToggle |
| **ui/** | Base components | Avatar, ConfirmDialog, VideoPlayer |
| **timeline/** | Chat visualization | ChatTimeline |

**Styling Approach:**
- **Tailwind CSS v4** with `@tailwindcss/postcss` plugin
- **CSS variables** for theming (light/dark modes)
- **Custom color palette**: accent (purple), foreground/background, surface/surface-hover, muted colors
- **Font optimization**: Geist Sans (main) + Geist Mono (code) from Next.js fonts
- **Utility classes**: Uses `cn()` helper (clsx + tailwind-merge) for conditional styling

**Animations:**
- **Framer Motion** for component animations and transitions

### 6. CUSTOM UTILITIES AND HOOKS

**useAuth Hook** (`hooks/use-auth.ts`)
- Wraps Supabase auth subscription
- Returns `{ user, profile, loading }`
- Fetches profile data on auth state change
- Cleanup subscription on unmount

**useGuideBuilder Hook** (`hooks/use-guide-builder.tsx`)
- Complex reducer pattern for guide builder state
- Manages metadata, blocks, steps, and block-to-step assignments
- Actions for: metadata updates, block imports, step CRUD, reordering, block assignments
- Display mode management (full, collapsed, trimmed, ghost)
- Author notes on blocks

**Utility Functions** (`lib/utils.ts`)
- `cn()`: Tailwind class merging
- `formatNumber()`: Converts numbers to K/M format
- `formatRelativeTime()`: Human-readable relative time ("2h ago")
- `slugify()`: URL-safe slugs from titles
- `guideDetailPath()`: Generates guide detail URL
- `formatJoinDate()`: User join date formatting

**Parser Utilities** (`lib/parser/claude-code.ts`)
- `parseClaudeCodeJsonl()`: Parses Claude Code JSONL conversation format
- Extracts text, tool actions (Create, Write), and file paths
- Handles XML tag stripping from system messages
- Filters out tool results and thinking blocks
- Converts user→human, assistant→assistant

### 7. API & SERVER ACTIONS

**No traditional REST API routes** - instead uses:
- **Supabase client** directly from browser
- **Server actions** in `lib/supabase/auth.ts` for authentication
- **Direct database queries** from components

**Auth Server Actions:**
- `signUp(formData)`: Create account with email/password/username
- `signIn(formData)`: Login with credentials
- `signOut()`: Clear session

**Supabase Query Functions:**
- Read operations: `fetchGuides()`, `fetchGuideById()`, `fetchProfile()`, etc.
- Write operations: `createGuide()`, `updateGuide()`, `createComment()`, etc.
- Toggle operations: `toggleLike()`, `toggleSave()`, `toggleFollow()`, `toggleStar()`, etc.

### 8. DATA FLOW EXAMPLE: Creating a Guide

1. User fills GuideBuilder form (manages state via useGuideBuilder)
2. Form captures: metadata, media files, parsed chat blocks, steps
3. On submit → calls `createGuide(input)` server function
4. Server function:
   - Inserts post record
   - Uploads media files to Supabase Storage
   - Inserts media references to `post_media` table
   - Batch inserts chat messages to `chat_messages` table (500 at a time)
5. Returns post ID
6. Redirects to new guide detail page

### 9. UNIQUE FEATURES

- **Claude Code Integration**: Special parser for Claude Code JSONL conversation exports
- **Timeline-based guides**: Guides shown as interactive chat conversations with chapters
- **Block categorization**: Auto-categorizes blocks as scaffold, feature, bug fix, refactor, etc.
- **Step blocks**: Maps conversation blocks to guide steps with display modes
- **Message annotations**: Authors can annotate/explain specific messages
- **Vibe-coded guides**: Flag for guides that feel more conversational/exploratory
- **Nested comments**: Comment depth tracking for threaded discussions

---

This architecture is well-suited for a collaborative guide-building platform focused on AI development workflows. The heavy use of Supabase for both auth and data storage, combined with Tailwind CSS for styling, provides a modern, scalable foundation. The guide builder's complex state management via useReducer shows careful attention to UX for power users creating multi-step guides.

│   │   ├── server.ts           # Server-side Supabase client

│   │   ├── middleware.ts       # Middleware for session updates
│   │   └── queries/

```

### 2. KEY ARCHITECTURAL PATTERNS

**Routing Architecture:**
- **App Router** (Modern): The primary routing system using directory-based routing in `app/`
- **Dynamic Routes**: Heavy use of `[params]` for IDs and slugs (e.g., `guide/[guideId]/[slug]`)
- **Route Groups**: Uses `(auth)` syntax for logical grouping of related routes
- **Client Components**: Most pages use `"use client"` for interactivity

**Data Fetching Patterns:**
- **Client-side fetching**: Pages use `useEffect` + state management for data in client components
- **Direct Supabase queries**: Browser client used directly from client components (potential performance concern for large datasets)
- **Server actions**: Auth operations (`signUp`, `signIn`, `signOut`) are server actions
- **Batch operations**: Large data inserts chunked in batches of 500

**State Management:**
- **React Context + useReducer**: `useGuideBuilder` hook for complex form state with nested steps/blocks
- **Local state with useState**: Used for UI state (sorting, loading, filters)
- **Custom hook abstraction**: `useAuth` encapsulates Supabase auth subscription logic

### 3. IMPORTANT CONFIGURATION FILES

**next.config.ts**
- Minimal configuration (currently empty/default)
- TypeScript configured for strict mode

**tsconfig.json**
- **Path alias**: `@/*` maps to `./src/*` for clean imports
- **Strict mode**: Enabled for type safety
- **Target**: ES2017 with React JSX transform
- **Module resolution**: bundler strategy

**eslint.config.mjs**
- Uses ESLint 9 with flat config
- Includes Next.js Core Web Vitals rules
- Includes TypeScript support
- Ignores `.next/`, `out/`, `build/`, `next-env.d.ts`

**postcss.config.mjs**
- Single plugin: `@tailwindcss/postcss` (Tailwind v4)

**Package.json Dependencies:**
- **Next.js 16.1.6**: Latest stable version with React 19.2.3
- **Supabase**: `@supabase/supabase-js` (client) + `@supabase/ssr` (server-side auth)
- **UI/Styling**: Tailwind CSS v4, Framer Motion, Lucide React icons, next-themes
- **Utilities**: clsx, tailwind-merge (for className merging)

### 4. SUPABASE INTEGRATION

**Authentication:**
- **Browser client** (`client.ts`): Singleton pattern for client-side operations
- **Server client** (`server.ts`): Cookie-based session management for server components
- **Middleware integration** (`middleware.ts`): Session validation on every request with cookie handling
- **Auth actions** (`auth.ts`): Server-side functions for `signUp`, `signIn`, `signOut`
- **Custom hook** (`useAuth`): Manages user state + profile loading with subscription cleanup

**Database Access Patterns:**
- **Type-safe queries**: Uses auto-generated `Database` type from Supabase
- **Nested queries**: Joins profiles, categories, media using Supabase's PostgREST syntax
- **Sorting**: Multiple sort options (recent, popular, trending, completed)
- **Pagination**: Limit-based pagination (currently 24 guides per page)
- **Batch operations**: Chunked inserts for large chat message batches
- **Soft deletes**: Uses `is_hidden` flag instead of hard deletes

**Core Database Tables:**
- **posts**: Main guide/content storage
- **profiles**: User information
- **categories**: Guide categories with icons
- **guide_steps**: Step-based guide structure
- **guide_blocks**: Parsed chat/code blocks from conversations
- **chat_messages**: Timeline of AI/human messages
- **comments**: Threaded comments with depth tracking
- **post_likes, post_saves, comment_likes**: Social interaction tracking
- **follows**: User follow relationships
- **post_media**: Images/videos associated with guides
- **timeline_chapters**: Named sections within guide timelines
- **message_annotations**: Author notes on specific messages
- **message_stars**: Starred messages in timelines

**Storage:**
- **Supabase Storage**: `post-media` bucket for guide images/videos
- **URL pattern**: `{userId}/{postId}/{mediaIndex}.{ext}`

### 5. COMPONENT ORGANIZATION

**Component Categories:**

| Category | Purpose | Example Files |
|----------|---------|----------------|
| **layout/** | App structure & navigation | AppShell, Navbar, Sidebar |
| **gallery/** | Guide browsing & discovery | GuideGrid, GuideCard, SortTabs |
| **create/** | Complex form builder | GuideBuilder, StepList, BlockPool |
| **guide/** | Guide viewing & interactions | GuidActions, Recommendations, MediaGallery |
| **comments/** | Discussion threads | CommentItem, CommentSection |
| **profile/** | User profiles | ProfileHeader, ProfileTabs, CommentList |
| **theme/** | Dark/light mode | ThemeProvider, ThemeToggle |
| **ui/** | Base components | Avatar, ConfirmDialog, VideoPlayer |
| **timeline/** | Chat visualization | ChatTimeline |

**Styling Approach:**
- **Tailwind CSS v4** with `@tailwindcss/postcss` plugin
- **CSS variables** for theming (light/dark modes)
- **Custom color palette**: accent (purple), foreground/background, surface/surface-hover, muted colors
- **Font optimization**: Geist Sans (main) + Geist Mono (code) from Next.js fonts
- **Utility classes**: Uses `cn()` helper (clsx + tailwind-merge) for conditional styling

**Animations:**
- **Framer Motion** for component animations and transitions

### 6. CUSTOM UTILITIES AND HOOKS

**useAuth Hook** (`hooks/use-auth.ts`)
- Wraps Supabase auth subscription
- Returns `{ user, profile, loading }`
- Fetches profile data on auth state change
- Cleanup subscription on unmount

**useGuideBuilder Hook** (`hooks/use-guide-builder.tsx`)
- Complex reducer pattern for guide builder state
- Manages metadata, blocks, steps, and block-to-step assignments
- Actions for: metadata updates, block imports, step CRUD, reordering, block assignments
- Display mode management (full, collapsed, trimmed, ghost)
- Author notes on blocks

**Utility Functions** (`lib/utils.ts`)
- `cn()`: Tailwind class merging
- `formatNumber()`: Converts numbers to K/M format
- `formatRelativeTime()`: Human-readable relative time ("2h ago")
- `slugify()`: URL-safe slugs from titles
- `guideDetailPath()`: Generates guide detail URL
- `formatJoinDate()`: User join date formatting

**Parser Utilities** (`lib/parser/claude-code.ts`)
- `parseClaudeCodeJsonl()`: Parses Claude Code JSONL conversation format
- Extracts text, tool actions (Create, Write), and file paths
- Handles XML tag stripping from system messages
- Filters out tool results and thinking blocks
- Converts user→human, assistant→assistant

### 7. API & SERVER ACTIONS

**No traditional REST API routes** - instead uses:
- **Supabase client** directly from browser
- **Server actions** in `lib/supabase/auth.ts` for authentication
- **Direct database queries** from components

**Auth Server Actions:**
- `signUp(formData)`: Create account with email/password/username
- `signIn(formData)`: Login with credentials
- `signOut()`: Clear session

**Supabase Query Functions:**
- Read operations: `fetchGuides()`, `fetchGuideById()`, `fetchProfile()`, etc.
- Write operations: `createGuide()`, `updateGuide()`, `createComment()`, etc.
- Toggle operations: `toggleLike()`, `toggleSave()`, `toggleFollow()`, `toggleStar()`, etc.

### 8. DATA FLOW EXAMPLE: Creating a Guide

1. User fills GuideBuilder form (manages state via useGuideBuilder)
2. Form captures: metadata, media files, parsed chat blocks, steps
3. On submit → calls `createGuide(input)` server function
4. Server function:
   - Inserts post record
   - Uploads media files to Supabase Storage
   - Inserts media references to `post_media` table
   - Batch inserts chat messages to `chat_messages` table (500 at a time)
5. Returns post ID
6. Redirects to new guide detail page

### 9. UNIQUE FEATURES

- **Claude Code Integration**: Special parser for Claude Code JSONL conversation exports
- **Timeline-based guides**: Guides shown as interactive chat conversations with chapters
- **Block categorization**: Auto-categorizes blocks as scaffold, feature, bug fix, refactor, etc.
- **Step blocks**: Maps conversation blocks to guide steps with display modes
- **Message annotations**: Authors can annotate/explain specific messages
- **Vibe-coded guides**: Flag for guides that feel more conversational/exploratory
- **Nested comments**: Comment depth tracking for threaded discussions

---

This architecture is well-suited for a collaborative guide-building platform focused on AI development workflows. The heavy use of Supabase for both auth and data storage, combined with Tailwind CSS for styling, provides a modern, scalable foundation. The guide builder's complex state management via useReducer shows careful attention to UX for power users creating multi-step guides.

   188→CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.update_guide_completion_stats()
   189→RETURNS trigger AS $$
   190→BEGIN
   191→  IF (tg_op = 'INSERT') THEN
   192→    UPDATE public.posts SET
   193→      completions_count = completions_count + 1,
   194→      avg_rating = (
   195→        SELECT ROUND(AVG(rating)::numeric, 2)
   196→        FROM public.guide_completions
   197→        WHERE post_id = NEW.post_id AND rating IS NOT NULL
   198→      )
   199→    WHERE id = NEW.post_id;
   200→    RETURN NEW;
   201→  ELSIF (tg_op = 'DELETE') THEN
   202→    UPDATE public.posts SET
   203→      completions_count = GREATEST(completions_count - 1, 0),
   204→      avg_rating = (
   205→        SELECT ROUND(AVG(rating)::numeric, 2)
   206→        FROM public.guide_completions
   207→        WHERE post_id = OLD.post_id AND rating IS NOT NULL
   208→      )
   209→    WHERE id = OLD.post_id;
   210→    RETURN OLD;
   211→  ELSIF (tg_op = 'UPDATE') THEN
   212→    UPDATE public.posts SET
   213→      avg_rating = (
   214→        SELECT ROUND(AVG(rating)::numeric, 2)
   215→        FROM public.guide_completions
   216→        WHERE post_id = NEW.post_id AND rating IS NOT NULL
   217→      )
   218→    WHERE id = NEW.post_id;
   219→    RETURN NEW;
   220→  END IF;
   221→  RETURN NULL;
   222→END;
   223→$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER;
   224→
   225→CREATE TRIGGER on_guide_completion_change
   226→  AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE ON public.guide_completions
   227→  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION public.update_guide_completion_stats();

   191→  IF (tg_op = 'INSERT') THEN
   192→    UPDATE public.posts SET
   193→      completions_count = completions_count + 1,
   194→      avg_rating = (
   195→        SELECT ROUND(AVG(rating)::numeric, 2)
   196→        FROM public.guide_completions
   197→        WHERE post_id = NEW.post_id AND rating IS NOT NULL
   198→      )
   199→    WHERE id = NEW.post_id;
   200→    RETURN NEW;
   201→  ELSIF (tg_op = 'DELETE') THEN
   202→    UPDATE public.posts SET
   203→      completions_count = GREATEST(completions_count - 1, 0),
   204→      avg_rating = (
   205→        SELECT ROUND(AVG(rating)::numeric, 2)
   206→        FROM public.guide_completions
   207→        WHERE post_id = OLD.post_id AND rating IS NOT NULL
   208→      )
   209→    WHERE id = OLD.post_id;
   210→    RETURN OLD;
   211→  ELSIF (tg_op = 'UPDATE') THEN
   212→    UPDATE public.posts SET
   213→      avg_rating = (
   214→        SELECT ROUND(AVG(rating)::numeric, 2)
   215→        FROM public.guide_completions
   216→        WHERE post_id = NEW.post_id AND rating IS NOT NULL
   217→      )
   218→    WHERE id = NEW.post_id;
   219→    RETURN NEW;
   220→  END IF;
   221→  RETURN NULL;
   222→END;
   223→$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER;
   224→
   225→CREATE TRIGGER on_guide_completion_change
   226→  AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE ON public.guide_completions
   227→  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION public.update_guide_completion_stats();

   188→CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.update_guide_completion_stats()
   189→RETURNS trigger AS $$
   190→BEGIN
   191→  IF (tg_op = 'INSERT') THEN
   192→    UPDATE public.posts SET
   193→      completions_count = completions_count + 1,
   194→      avg_rating = (
   195→        SELECT ROUND(AVG(rating)::numeric, 2)
   196→        FROM public.guide_completions
   197→        WHERE post_id = NEW.post_id AND rating IS NOT NULL
   198→      )
   199→    WHERE id = NEW.post_id;
   200→    RETURN NEW;
   201→  ELSIF (tg_op = 'DELETE') THEN
   202→    UPDATE public.posts SET
   203→      completions_count = GREATEST(completions_count - 1, 0),
   204→      avg_rating = (
   205→        SELECT ROUND(AVG(rating)::numeric, 2)
   206→        FROM public.guide_completions
   207→        WHERE post_id = OLD.post_id AND rating IS NOT NULL
   208→      )
   209→    WHERE id = OLD.post_id;
   210→    RETURN OLD;
   211→  ELSIF (tg_op = 'UPDATE') THEN
   212→    UPDATE public.posts SET
   213→      avg_rating = (
   214→        SELECT ROUND(AVG(rating)::numeric, 2)
   215→        FROM public.guide_completions
   216→        WHERE post_id = NEW.post_id AND rating IS NOT NULL
   217→      )
   218→    WHERE id = NEW.post_id;
   219→    RETURN NEW;
   220→  END IF;
   221→  RETURN NULL;
   222→END;
   223→$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER;
   224→
   225→CREATE TRIGGER on_guide_completion_change
   226→  AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE ON public.guide_completions
   227→  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION public.update_guide_completion_stats();

## Supabase Query Performance Analysis Report

Based on my thorough exploration of the Supabase queries and client configuration, I've identified several significant performance optimization opportunities:

---

## 1. OVER-SELECTING COLUMNS (Unnecessary Data Transfers)

### Issue: fetchGuides() - Line 11-15 in guides.ts
**File:** `C:\Users\Seba\Documents\pathway-20260219T010633Z-1-001\pathway\src\lib\supabase\queries\guides.ts`

```typescript
select(`
  *,
  profile:profiles!posts_user_id_fkey(*),
  media:post_media(*)
`)
```

**Problem:** Fetching ALL columns from posts, profiles, and post_media tables. This includes unnecessary columns like:
- `posts.original_json` (potentially large)
- `posts.what_youll_build` 
- `profiles.*` (including bio, credentials URLs, etc.)
- All post_media fields including URLs

**Impact:** Each of 24 guides (limit on line 35) loads full nested data. For a list view, you typically only need `id, title, description, user_id, likes_count, created_at, avatar_url, username` for the profile.

---

### Issue: fetchGuideById() - Line 9-16 in guide-detail.ts
**File:** `C:\Users\Seba\Documents\pathway-20260219T010633Z-1-001\pathway\src\lib\supabase\queries\guide-detail.ts`

```typescript
select(`
  *,
  profile:profiles!posts_user_id_fkey(*),
  category:categories!posts_category_id_fkey(*),
  media:post_media(*),
  chat_messages(*, annotation:message_annotations(*), star:message_stars(*)),
  timeline_chapters(*)
`)
```

**Problem:** Fetches EVERYTHING including potentially thousands of chat messages with their annotations and star data. This is massive for large guides.

---

### Issue: fetchUserGuides(), fetchUserLikedGuides(), fetchUserSavedGuides() - Lines 22-26, 58-64, 77-83 in profile.ts
**File:** `C:\Users\Seba\Documents\pathway-20260219T010633Z-1-001\pathway\src\lib\supabase\queries\profile.ts`

**Problem:** All selecting `*` from profiles for every guide in user collections. For profile views loading multiple guides, this compounds the data transfer.

---

## 2. N+1 QUERY PATTERNS

### Issue: Status Checks on Guide Detail Page - Lines 70-88 in [guideId]/[slug]/page.tsx
**File:** `C:\Users\Seba\Documents\pathway-20260219T010633Z-1-001\pathway\src\app\guide\[guideId]\[slug]\page.tsx`

```typescript
// Three separate queries after fetching the guide
const [likeStatus, saveStatus, followStatus] = await Promise.all([
  checkLikeStatus(guide!.id, user!.id),      // Query 1: post_likes
  checkSaveStatus(guide!.id, user!.id),      // Query 2: post_saves
  guide!.profile && guide!.user_id !== user!.id
    ? checkFollowStatus(user!.id, guide!.user_id)  // Query 3: follows
    : Promise.resolve(false),
]);
```

**Problem:** Three separate queries could be combined into one or use batch fetch. The `checkFollowStatus()` (line 141-152 in guide-detail.ts) queries the `follows` table with two equality filters - this doesn't need a separate roundtrip.

---

### Issue: Profile Tab Data Loading - Lines 55-78 in profile/[username]/page.tsx
**File:** `C:\Users\Seba\Documents\pathway-20260219T010633Z-1-001\pathway\src\app\profile\[username]\page.tsx`

```typescript
switch (activeTab) {
  case "guides":
    data = await fetchUserGuides(profile!.id);      // Query 1
    break;
  case "comments":
    data = await fetchUserComments(profile!.id);    // Query 2
    break;
  case "liked":
    data = await fetchUserLikedGuides(profile!.id); // Query 3
    break;
  case "saved":
    data = await fetchUserSavedGuides(profile!.id); // Query 4
    break;
}
```

**Problem:** Not truly N+1 in this case (sequential single queries), but the comment list triggers another nested query in fetchUserComments (lines 40-51 in profile.ts) which joins profiles AND posts:

```typescript
select(`
  *,
  profile:profiles!comments_user_id_fkey(*),
  post:posts!comments_post_id_fkey(id, title)
`)
```

Each comment loads full profile data.

---

## 3. PAGINATION NOT IMPLEMENTED

### Issue: fetchGuides() - Line 35 in guides.ts
**File:** `C:\Users\Seba\Documents\pathway-20260219T010633Z-1-001\pathway\src\lib\supabase\queries\guides.ts`

```typescript
const { data, error } = await query.limit(24);
```

**Problem:** Hard-coded limit of 24 with NO offset/pagination support. When users want more guides, the entire list reloads. No infinite scroll or pagination API.

---

### Issue: fetchUserGuides(), fetchUserComments(), fetchUserLikedGuides(), fetchUserSavedGuides() - Lines 17-89 in profile.ts
**File:** `C:\Users\Seba\Documents\pathway-20260219T010633Z-1-001\pathway\src\lib\supabase\queries\profile.ts`

**Problem:** All three functions have NO limit and NO pagination:
- Line 21-26: `fetchUserGuides()` - No `.limit()` call
- Line 38-47: `fetchUserComments()` - No `.limit()` call  
- Line 56-70: `fetchUserLikedGuides()` - No `.limit()` call
- Line 75-88: `fetchUserSavedGuides()` - No `.limit()` call

**Impact:** If a user has 500 guides, ALL 500 load into memory and are fetched across the network.

---

### Issue: fetchGuideComments() - Line 58-73 in guide-detail.ts
**File:** `C:\Users\Seba\Documents\pathway-20260219T010633Z-1-001\pathway\src\lib\supabase\queries\guide-detail.ts`

```typescript
const { data, error } = await supabase
  .from("comments")
  .select(`
    *,
    profile:profiles!comments_user_id_fkey(*)
  `)
  .eq("post_id", guideId)
  .eq("is_hidden", false)
  .order("created_at", { ascending: true });
  // NO .limit() call
```

**Problem:** No pagination. Popular guides with 1000+ comments load all of them at once.

---

## 4. QUERY CACHING OPPORTUNITIES

### Issue: No Client-Side Caching Strategy
**Problem:** Every time a user visits a page, full re-fetches happen:
- Profile pages (line 39 in profile/[username]/page.tsx): `fetchProfileByUsername()` always refetches
- Guide detail (line 44 in [guideId]/[slug]/page.tsx): `fetchGuideById()` always refetches
- Status checks (lines 74-80 in [guideId]/[slug]/page.tsx): Always refetch like/save/follow status

**Opportunity:** Implement React Query / SWR with cache invalidation.

---

### Issue: Recommended Guides Query - Line 164-187 in guide-detail.ts
**File:** `C:\Users\Seba\Documents\pathway-20260219T010633Z-1-001\pathway\src\lib\supabase\queries\guide-detail.ts`

```typescript
export async function fetchRecommendedGuides(guideId: string, categoryId: string | null): Promise<any[]> {
  // Always fresh query - no caching
  const { data, error } = await query;
  // ...
}
```

**Problem:** Recommendations recalculate on every guide view. Could cache category recommendations for 1-2 minutes.

---

## 5. INEFFICIENT JOINS & AGGREGATIONS

### Issue: fetchUserComments() Double Profile Load - Lines 40-51 in profile.ts
**File:** `C:\Users\Seba\Documents\pathway-20260219T010633Z-1-001\pathway\src\lib\supabase\queries\profile.ts`

```typescript
select(`
  *,
  profile:profiles!comments_user_id_fkey(*),    // Full profile (but we already know user_id)
  post:posts!comments_post_id_fkey(id, title)   // Only id and title needed
`)
```

**Problem:** Loads full profile (avatar_url, bio, etc.) for every comment, even though you're viewing a specific user's comments - you already know who the commenter is.

---

### Issue: Chat Messages with Annotations - Line 14 in guide-detail.ts
**File:** `C:\Users\Seba\Documents\pathway-20260219T010633Z-1-001\pathway\src\lib\supabase\queries\guide-detail.ts`

```typescript
chat_messages(*, annotation:message_annotations(*), star:message_stars(*)),
```

**Problem:** For a guide with 500 chat messages:
- Joins 500+ `message_annotations` rows (1:many)
- Joins 500+ `message_stars` rows (1:many)
- Line 30-36 then filters these in JavaScript with array processing

**Impact:** Database returns massive result set that needs client-side filtering.

---

### Issue: Media Sorting in Client Code - Lines 24-26 in guide-detail.ts
**File:** `C:\Users\Seba\Documents\pathway-20260219T010633Z-1-001\pathway\src\lib\supabase\queries\guide-detail.ts`

```typescript
if (data.media) {
  (data.media as any[]).sort((a: any, b: any) => a.order - b.order);
}
```

**Problem:** Fetch returns unordered media, then sorts in JavaScript. Should order in SQL: `.select(...).order("order", { ascending: true })`

Same for chat_messages (line 28) and timeline_chapters (line 39).

---

## 6. CLIENT CONFIGURATION ISSUES

### Issue: No Pooling or Request Batching in Client Setup
**File:** `C:\Users\Seba\Documents\pathway-20260219T010633Z-1-001\pathway\src\lib\supabase\client.ts`

```typescript
export function createClient() {
  if (client) return client;
  client = createBrowserClient<Database>(
    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL!,
    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY!
  );
  return client;
}
```

**Problem:** 
- No batch query support configuration
- No connection pooling settings
- No request deduplication
- No retry strategy

---

### Issue: Server Client Missing Middleware
**File:** `C:\Users\Seba\Documents\pathway-20260219T010633Z-1-001\pathway\src\lib\supabase\server.ts`

```typescript
const { cookies } = "next/headers";
// ...
return createServerClient(
  process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL!,
  process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY!,
  {
    cookies: { /* ... */ }
  }
);
```

**Missing:**
- No session token refresh strategy
- No edge function caching headers
- No response cache hints

---

## 7. MEDIA UPLOAD SEQUENTIAL OPERATIONS

### Issue: createGuide() and publishGuide() Media Upload - Lines 80-104 in guides.ts and Lines 43-67 in create-guide.ts
**File:** `C:\Users\Seba\Documents\pathway-20260219T010633Z-1-001\pathway\src\lib\supabase\queries\guides.ts`

```typescript
for (let i = 0; i < input.mediaFiles.length; i++) {
  const media = input.mediaFiles[i];
  // ... sequential upload and URL fetch
  const { error: uploadError } = await supabase.storage
    .from("post-media")
    .upload(path, media.file);
  
  const { data: urlData } = supabase.storage
    .from("post-media")
    .getPublicUrl(path);
}
```

**Problem:** Sequential loop. Should use `Promise.all()` for parallel uploads.

---

## 8. MISSING INDEXES

Based on schema analysis, these indexes are missing but heavily queried:

### Missing in posts table:
- `post_media.post_id` (used in every guide detail fetch) - EXISTS: `idx_chat_messages_post_id`
- No composite index on `(is_hidden, trending_score)` for filtering + sorting

### Missing in likes/saves:
- No query-friendly index on `(post_id, user_id)` for batch status checks
- `post_likes` and `post_saves` use composite PK but could benefit from `(user_id, post_id)` for "my likes"

### Missing in follows:
- Both ways covered: `(follower_id)` and `(following_id)` exist

---

## SUMMARY TABLE

| Issue | Severity | Location | Impact |
|-------|----------|----------|--------|
| Over-selecting columns | HIGH | guides.ts:11-15, guide-detail.ts:9-16, profile.ts | Data transfer, memory |
| No pagination | HIGH | guides.ts:35, profile.ts:17-89, guide-detail.ts:58-73 | Scalability, memory |
| Status checks N+1 | MEDIUM | [guideId]/page.tsx:70-88 | 3 queries instead of 1 |
| Chat messages joins | MEDIUM | guide-detail.ts:14 | Database load, transfer size |
| Client-side sorting | LOW | guide-detail.ts:24-40 | Processing overhead |
| Sequential media uploads | MEDIUM | guides.ts:80-104, create-guide.ts:43-67 | Upload time |
| No caching strategy | HIGH | Multiple pages | Repeated fetches |
| Missing index on media | MEDIUM | Schema | Query performance |

---

## QUICK WINS (Easiest to Implement)

1. **Add pagination parameters** to `fetchGuides()`, `fetchUserGuides()`, etc.
2. **Remove `.order()` in JavaScript** - move to SQL ordering
3. **Specify column selections** instead of `*` in all queries
4. **Parallel media uploads** using `Promise.all()`
5. **Cache status checks** in React component state

**Problem:** Three separate queries could be combined into one or use batch fetch. The `checkFollowStatus()` (line 141-152 in guide-detail.ts) queries the `follows` table with two equality filters - this doesn't need a separate roundtrip.

**File:** `C:\Users\Seba\Documents\pathway-20260219T010633Z-1-001\pathway\src\lib\supabase\queries\guides.ts`

Based on schema analysis, these indexes are missing but heavily queried:

- `post_media.post_id` (used in every guide detail fetch) - EXISTS: `idx_chat_messages_post_id`

# Performance Plan: Server-Side Data Fetching

## Problem
All pages use `"use client"` with `useEffect` for data fetching, causing:
- Blank screen → spinner → content (poor UX)
- No SEO benefits (content not in initial HTML)
- Waterfall requests (auth check → data fetch → render)

## Solution
Convert key pages to Server Components with server-side data fetching. Interactive parts become separate client components.

## Changes

### 1. Home Page (`src/app/page.tsx`)

**Current:** Client component with useEffect fetching guides
**After:** Server component that fetches guides, passes to client `<ExploreClient>` for interactivity (sort/search)

Files to modify:
- `src/app/page.tsx` - Convert to async Server Component
- `src/components/gallery/ExploreClient.tsx` - New client component for interactivity

```
// page.tsx (Server Component)
export default async function ExplorePage({ searchParams }) {
  const sort = searchParams.sort || "trending";
  const query = searchParams.query || "";
  const guides = await fetchGuides(sort, query);
  return <ExploreClient initialGuides={guides} initialSort={sort} initialQuery={query} />;
}
```

### 2. Guide Detail (`src/app/guide/[guideId]/[slug]/page.tsx`)

**Current:** Client component with dual useEffect (guide data + user status)
**After:** Server component fetches guide/comments/recommended; client component handles user status + interactions

Files to modify:
- `src/app/guide/[guideId]/[slug]/page.tsx` - Convert to async Server Component
- `src/components/guide/GuidePageClient.tsx` - New client component for interactions

### 3. Profile Page (`src/app/profile/[username]/page.tsx`)

**Current:** Client component with lazy-loaded tabs
**After:** Server component fetches profile + initial tab data; client handles tab switching

Files to modify:
- `src/app/profile/[username]/page.tsx` - Convert to async Server Component
- `src/components/profile/ProfileClient.tsx` - New client component for tabs

### 4. Loading States

Add `loading.tsx` files for Suspense-based loading:
- `src/app/loading.tsx`
- `src/app/guide/[guideId]/[slug]/loading.tsx`
- `src/app/profile/[username]/loading.tsx`

## Verification

1. Run `npm run build` - should complete without errors
2. Run `npm run dev` and test:
   - Home page loads guides immediately (no spinner flash)
   - Guide detail shows content on initial load
   - Profile page shows profile + guides on initial load
   - View page source to confirm HTML contains actual content (SEO)
3. Check Network tab - initial page load should include data, not require separate fetch

- The queries currently use the browser client - will they work with server client?
- How to handle user-specific data (like status checks) that requires the current user

   - Currently: useEffect fetches guide + comments + recommended, second useEffect checks user's like/save/follow status

   - Needs: Server fetch for profile + initial tab, client component for tab switching

1. The exact structure of the Server Component (what it fetches, what props it passes)
2. What the new client component should handle

4. Any gotchas with the current query functions (do they need server versions?)

Also consider:
- The queries currently use the browser client - will they work with server client?
- How to handle user-specific data (like status checks) that requires the current user
- Loading.tsx placement for Suspense boundaries

# Performance Plan: Server-Side Data Fetching

## Problem
All pages use `"use client"` with `useEffect` for data fetching, causing:
- Blank screen → spinner → content (poor UX)
- No SEO benefits (content not in initial HTML)
- Waterfall requests (auth check → data fetch → render)

## Solution
Convert key pages to Server Components with server-side data fetching. Interactive parts become separate client components.

## Changes

### 1. Home Page (`src/app/page.tsx`)

**Current:** Client component with useEffect fetching guides
**After:** Server component that fetches guides, passes to client `<ExploreClient>` for interactivity (sort/search)

Files to modify:
- `src/app/page.tsx` - Convert to async Server Component
- `src/components/gallery/ExploreClient.tsx` - New client component for interactivity

```
// page.tsx (Server Component)
export default async function ExplorePage({ searchParams }) {
  const sort = searchParams.sort || "trending";
  const query = searchParams.query || "";
  const guides = await fetchGuides(sort, query);
  return <ExploreClient initialGuides={guides} initialSort={sort} initialQuery={query} />;
}
```

### 2. Guide Detail (`src/app/guide/[guideId]/[slug]/page.tsx`)

**Current:** Client component with dual useEffect (guide data + user status)
**After:** Server component fetches guide/comments/recommended; client component handles user status + interactions

Files to modify:
- `src/app/guide/[guideId]/[slug]/page.tsx` - Convert to async Server Component
- `src/components/guide/GuidePageClient.tsx` - New client component for interactions

### 3. Profile Page (`src/app/profile/[username]/page.tsx`)

**Current:** Client component with lazy-loaded tabs
**After:** Server component fetches profile + initial tab data; client handles tab switching

Files to modify:
- `src/app/profile/[username]/page.tsx` - Convert to async Server Component
- `src/components/profile/ProfileClient.tsx` - New client component for tabs

### 4. Loading States

Add `loading.tsx` files for Suspense-based loading:
- `src/app/loading.tsx`
- `src/app/guide/[guideId]/[slug]/loading.tsx`
- `src/app/profile/[username]/loading.tsx`

## Verification

1. Run `npm run build` - should complete without errors
2. Run `npm run dev` and test:
   - Home page loads guides immediately (no spinner flash)
   - Guide detail shows content on initial load
   - Profile page shows profile + guides on initial load
   - View page source to confirm HTML contains actual content (SEO)
3. Check Network tab - initial page load should include data, not require separate fetch

- Blank screen → spinner → content (poor UX)
- No SEO benefits (content not in initial HTML)
- Waterfall requests (auth check → data fetch → render)

## Solution
Convert key pages to Server Components with server-side data fetching. Interactive parts become separate client components.

## Changes

### 1. Home Page (`src/app/page.tsx`)

**Current:** Client component with useEffect fetching guides
**After:** Server component that fetches guides, passes to client `<ExploreClient>` for interactivity (sort/search)

Files to modify:
- `src/app/page.tsx` - Convert to async Server Component
- `src/components/gallery/ExploreClient.tsx` - New client component for interactivity

```
// page.tsx (Server Component)
export default async function ExplorePage({ searchParams }) {
  const sort = searchParams.sort || "trending";
  const query = searchParams.query || "";
  const guides = await fetchGuides(sort, query);
  return <ExploreClient initialGuides={guides} initialSort={sort} initialQuery={query} />;
}
```

### 2. Guide Detail (`src/app/guide/[guideId]/[slug]/page.tsx`)

**Current:** Client component with dual useEffect (guide data + user status)
**After:** Server component fetches guide/comments/recommended; client component handles user status + interactions

Files to modify:
- `src/app/guide/[guideId]/[slug]/page.tsx` - Convert to async Server Component
- `src/components/guide/GuidePageClient.tsx` - New client component for interactions

### 3. Profile Page (`src/app/profile/[username]/page.tsx`)

**Current:** Client component with lazy-loaded tabs
**After:** Server component fetches profile + initial tab data; client handles tab switching

Files to modify:
- `src/app/profile/[username]/page.tsx` - Convert to async Server Component
- `src/components/profile/ProfileClient.tsx` - New client component for tabs

### 4. Loading States

Add `loading.tsx` files for Suspense-based loading:
- `src/app/loading.tsx`
- `src/app/guide/[guideId]/[slug]/loading.tsx`
- `src/app/profile/[username]/loading.tsx`

## Verification

1. Run `npm run build` - should complete without errors
2. Run `npm run dev` and test:
   - Home page loads guides immediately (no spinner flash)
   - Guide detail shows content on initial load
   - Profile page shows profile + guides on initial load
   - View page source to confirm HTML contains actual content (SEO)
3. Check Network tab - initial page load should include data, not require separate fetch
